# DOT Reasonable Suspicion Drug and Alcohol Testing for Managers and Supervisors Training

> 2-hour online training for managers and supervisors of commercial motor vehicle drivers, based on DOT 49 CFR Part 40 and FMCSA 49 CFR Part 382. Available in English and Spanish. Offered by HAZWOPER OSHA Training (https://hazwoper-osha.com).

## Key facts
- Duration: 2 hours; 4 lessons, final exam
- Credits: 0.2 CEU
- Price: $49.99 per person; bulk pricing available
- Delivery: 100% online, 24/7; SCORM, virtual instructor-led and in-person formats also available
- Languages: English, Spanish
- Prerequisites: none
- Refresher: DOT sets no frequency; industry best practice is every two years
- Covers the FMCSA 60/60 supervisor training requirement (60 minutes alcohol misuse, 60 minutes controlled substances)

## Key concepts
- Reasonable suspicion observations must be specific, contemporaneous and articulable
- Indicators: physical, behavioral, speech and olfactory
- Five DOT drug classes: marijuana, cocaine, amphetamines, opioids, PCP
- Alcohol: 0.04 or greater is a violation; 0.02 to 0.039 requires removal from safety-sensitive functions for at least 24 hours
- Prescription controlled substances under 49 CFR 382.213
- FMCSA Clearinghouse II and SAP requirements after a violation

## Lessons
1. Regulatory Framework and the Reasonable Suspicion Standard
2. Indicators of Alcohol Misuse, BAC Thresholds and Immediate Actions
3. The Five DOT Drug Classes and Observable Impairment Indicators
4. Protocol, Confrontation, Refusals, and Clearinghouse II Mandates

## Who should take it
Managers and supervisors of CMV drivers; fleet, transportation and operations managers; staff supporting DOT drug and alcohol testing compliance; employers overseeing FMCSA-regulated safety-sensitive operations.
